coaching.headline: Two lanes were won clean, offlane over Crunch and jungle over Khaimera, but three others leaned the opponent's way the whole game, and five won fights turned into just two cashed objectives while towers fell 2 to 11. That conversion gap, not the draft, decided the game.
coaching.team: Two lanes read favored the whole game, offlane over Crunch and jungle over Khaimera, while carry, mid and support all leaned the opponent's way for most or all of the game. The start was clean: first blood at 3.4 minutes, Renna over Khaimera, with Maco adding a second kill moments later for a two-nothing lead. That lead was gone by the next fight, a full five-on-five taken in the enemy's side of the river at 4.8 minutes with no objective up, lost 1-4. Fangtooth fell to the enemy twice after that, at 11 and 18 minutes, each time with one of our own already dead going in, Greystone caught by Dekker before the first and Scarlett caught by Eden before the second. The team was also caught alone seven times over the game to the opponents' four, and Eden alone caught three of our players solo. Vision and river control both went the enemy's way: 40 wards placed to their 35, but we never destroyed a single enemy ward while they cleared six of ours, and river buffs split 9 to 17 in their favor with both Seedlings going to them too. The clearest single moment came at 27.7 minutes: Legion and Scarlett held Orb Prime two against two while Greystone, alive and ahead in his own lane, never rotated in to make it three against two. Greystone was then caught alone by Morigesh at 28.5 trying to get there late, and Orb Prime fell at 29 with him already dead. The one clean answer was the pickoff at 29.4: Renna and Greystone caught three enemies two-on-three at their Inhibitor and won it 3-0. The next fight, at 30.9, went 1-4 with Scarlett alive and never in it. Primal Fangtooth still fell in that same window, which blunted the loss, but an inhibitor and the core followed within the next two minutes and the game ended at 32. Next game's focus: close the seven-to-four caught-out gap by grouping up before crossing into contested space instead of rotating alone.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: What actually cost the game? At 27.7 minutes, Legion and Scarlett held Orb Prime two against two while Greystone, ahead in his own lane, never rotated in to flip it three against two. Orb Prime and two inhibitors were gone within the next two minutes, and towers finished the game 2 to 11 -- a deficit that was already building before this fight.
coaching.whatWorked: The pickoff at 29.4 minutes was the cleanest win of the game: Renna and Greystone caught three enemies two-on-three at their Inhibitor and won it 3-0; Primal Fangtooth actually fell in the same window as the fight the team lost 1-4 at 30.9.

The death at 25.4 minutes, alongside Renna, fed two inner towers within a minute, and the one at 31.2 opened the last inhibitor and the core that closed the game. Ten assists across the game is real map presence for a losing lane, but Vanguardian's armor and tenacity only finished an estimated 29 minutes in, well past where it would have helped most.

23.1.call: Splitting up worked here: Renna, Maco, Legion and Scarlett held our Outer Tower and won it 3-2 without Greystone, and the team took Fangtooth in that same window. That's a split worth repeating when the team already has the numbers to hold a fight without the jungler.

29.4.call: Renna and Greystone caught three enemies two-on-three at their Inhibitor and won it 3-0, the clearest proof the team could win outnumbered when the pick was right.

30.9.call: Scarlett was alive and never made this fight, effectively leaving it four against five before it started. Primal Fangtooth still fell in the same window across the map, which blunted the loss, but an inhibitor and the core followed within the next two minutes and the game ended shortly after.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Maco's build matched the full winning core, Crescelia, Enra's Blessing and Windcaller, all three built, all mana regeneration and heal-flex tools for the Gift! poke-and-heal kit. The fourth slot went to Vanguardian instead of continuing down the optimizer's path toward Noxia, Timewarp, Lifecore and Lunaria, all magical power and healing-power pieces that would have kept scaling the heal-flex; Vanguardian is tenacity and dual armor instead. That's a real trade: more raw power and heal output against Dekker's poke, or the tenacity and armor that helps survive being caught alone, which happened to Maco twice before ten minutes. Against a support lane that read Dekker's the whole game and caught Maco out twice before ten minutes, the tenacity pick has an argument, but Vanguardian didn't finish until an estimated 29 minutes in, well past where it mattered most.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Vesh is the top-fit pick for Maco, an ability-damage blessing that turns every landed ability hit into a damage-over-time tick, which suits a burst/utility support built around poking and flexing the heal into damage. The default minors, Tithe of Death for ability haste on takedowns and Mind Rot for bonus damage tied to the DoT, reward a support that keeps landing spells rather than one built to soak hits. The trade against this game specifically: Vesh adds damage pressure but nothing that would have helped Maco survive being caught alone by Eden inside the first eight minutes, when a more defensive, peel-first style would have paid off instead.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Legion's build stacked critical-strike chance across all four items, Vanquisher, Tainted Rounds, Nuclear Rounds and Terminus, plus the healing cut Tainted Rounds applies on hit. The winning core's other two pieces, Malady and Deathstalker, are both built around armor penetration instead, something this build only picked up in Vanquisher's own share. Against a lineup fronted by Crunch's tankiness, cutting through armor matters as much as raising crit chance does, and this build leaned hard toward the crit side of that trade.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Demiurge is Legion's top-fit pick, adding a flat boost to every item stat and to item-effect damage, which rewards a completed six-item build more than any single early item does. Legion finished only four items by the end of this 32-minute loss, so a chunk of that scaling never got realized. The alternative style, an on-hit blessing like Vermis that adds bonus damage every third auto-attack on the same target, pays out earlier in a fight and would have leaned into the crit-and-attack-speed build already on hand, trading Demiurge's late-game ceiling for damage that shows up sooner in an unfavored lane.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Scarlett's finished build ran tanky: Tainted Guard and Citadel for armor and health, Overlord for more health, and Syonic Echo and Terminus for lifesteal and crit on top. That matches the role Scarlett actually filled: the kit read lists Scarlett as the team's only true frontline. The optimizer's suggested path, Viper, The Perforator, Spear Of Desolation, Augmentation, Basilisk and Solaris, leans into armor penetration, ability haste and raw health rather than armor plating. Given the team had almost no hard crowd control to force a pick, having one body that could stand in a fight and survive it mattered, even if it meant less penetration into Crunch and the rest of the enemy frontline.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Krix is Scarlett's top-fit pick, a flat and growing max-health blessing that fits a hero built to stand in the fight and tank it. The default minors, Festering Wounds and Cannibalism, add a healing cut and permanent health on every takedown on top of that health stacking, both rewarding staying alive and staying in the fight rather than trading in and out. The alternative style is a dueling blessing like Thraex, which marks the last target Scarlett's basics hit for extra damage taken and dealt, better suited to a build already carrying 30% lifesteal; Krix is the safer pick for the team's only true frontline against a comp with a real dive threat in Crunch.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Greystone's three finished items, Sky Splitter, Lightning Hawk and Tainted Bastion, are almost entirely attack speed, crit chance and physical power, with only Tainted Bastion adding any defense, and that defense is magical armor, not physical. The build flag on this game is explicit: no physical armor against a lineup where three of five damage dealers, Khaimera, Eden and Crunch, hit physical. Greystone only finished three items by the 32-minute mark, fewest on the team, so a later armor purchase never arrived; the aggressive itemization fit the frontline-bruiser, front-and-reset kit in theory, but it left Greystone without the one stat that answers this specific enemy comp.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Krix, the same health-stacking blessing Scarlett's build points to, is also Greystone's top-fit pick, growing max health flat and by level rather than needing items to pay off. That suits a jungler who finished behind on gold and only completed three items this game, since Krix's value comes from leveling up, not from a full build. The alternative, Demiurge's item-scaling package, is the same blessing the engine picks for the rest of the team, but it needs the finished items Greystone never got to buy; Krix's frontline, reset-focused fit for the leap-in, stasis-heal kit holds up regardless of how the build itself went.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Renna's build matched two of the three meta-core items, Entropy for mana and magical power and Overseer for penetration and magical lifesteal, and swapped the third, Wraith Leggings, for Orb Of Enlightenment and Tainted Scepter instead. Wraith Leggings adds flat magical penetration and bonus damage against targets under 40% health, and it's the one item both the aggregate meta core and Renna's own optimizer path agree on. What was built instead, Orb Of Enlightenment's per-level health and mana growth plus a small heal on ability cast, and Tainted Scepter's healing cut, gave more sustain and mana, at the cost of the extra penetration and execute damage that would have helped close out fights against a comp Renna was already winning the damage race against.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Demiurge is also Renna's top-fit pick, the same item-scaling blessing that rewards a finished six-item build, which suits a late-scaling ability-power carry whose win condition is zoning a fight with Mortal Coil and the ultimate. Renna finished only four items in this loss, so that scaling engine was still building toward its payoff when the game ended. The alternative, Vesh's ability-damage blessing that leaves a damage-over-time tick on every spell hit, would have added more pressure earlier, in the skirmishes and lane trades Renna was already winning kills in before the midlane read turned unfavored.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~1.3s of lockdown): Crunch Right Crunch (knockup 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Dekker. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
Dive threat on our backline: Crunch. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Maco) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.
